subject: VPC implementation-gradient & volume discount pathway
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Laura Spencer <laura.spencer@medisphere.com>, Procurement <procurement@medisphere.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: VPC implementation-gradient & volume discount pathway

Laura / team —

Thanks again for the deep-dive yesterday. A few follow-ups from our side as you think about how to structure the commercial for a multi-site VPC rollout:

Quick context: Medisphere is targeting a pilot (2 sites) in Q3 and a scale phase (up to 8 sites) in H2. You asked for options that avoid a single large up-front platform fee while preserving predictable SRE/support coverage and a path to larger volume discounting.

High-level asks for you: can you confirm whether Medisphere prefers (A) amortized platform fee over 12 months or (B) a smaller platform fee + higher per-node consumption in the pilot period? That will materially change how we price the support retainer.

We're prepping two commercial routes and a short SOW draft; attaching a working pricing matrix and draft SOW for internal review. Key tradeoffs we want to call out:
- Option 1 (Anchor): lower per-node rates at scale, platform fee amortized across the committed sites, 24/7 on-call retainer at mid-tier SLA.
- Option 2 (Elastic): minimal anchor/platform fee, higher initial per-node and support retainer that steps down with volume bands.

If you can share target payment terms (Net30/45) and whether the platform fee must be capitalized this quarter, we will tune the amortization and payment milestones.

Attachments: redwood-privdeploy-pricing-matrix.xlsx (workbook), SOW-draft-v2.pdf (strawman)

Next steps: we’ll send an external-facing summary once Marissa finishes the two-option line items. Can we aim for a decision checkpoint by Friday 5/22?

Best,
David
David Kim
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Spencer <laura.spencer@medisphere.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: VPC implementation-gradient & volume discount pathway

David —

Thanks for the note and the attachments. Helpful framing. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Budget/timing: Finance prefers to avoid a large capital hit this quarter; amortization across 12 months is acceptable but we need a clear invoice schedule (milestone-driven is best).
2) Pilot constraints: Pilot cannot exceed $150k in cash burn in Q3. We may be able to commit to a scale option if pilot metrics meet latency/cost targets.
3) Support expectations: For pilot we only need weekday coverage with priority SLAs; for scale we’ll need 24/7 on-call. Can you show a migration path between the two without a full contract rewrite?

If you can send a short table that maps invoicing (milestone) to accounting treatment and the exact SRE coverage delta between pilot vs scale I can take to procurement.

Laura Spencer
Director, Cloud Infrastructure
Medisphere Health

Subject: Internal: pricing matrix (two-option) + SOW notes for Medisphere

Team —

I reviewed the constraints Laura laid out and updated the matrix. Key points in the attachment (redwood-privdeploy-pricing-matrix.xlsx):

Option A (Anchor / amortized):
- Platform fee: $420k amortized over 12 months (pilot invoice milestone 30%, remainder monthly).
- Node licensing: $3,500 / node / month at pilot scale (2 sites, 8 nodes), steps to $2,200 / node / month at 8+ sites.
- Support: Tier-2 retainer $18k / month during pilot; converts to Tier-3 (24/7) at scale with a $45k / month retainer.

Option B (Elastic / pay-as-you-go):
- Platform fee: $75k one-time (pilot cap), no amortization.
- Node licensing: $4,500 / node / month during pilot, volume discounts kick in after month 6 based on committed nodes.
- Support: higher baseline retainer $28k / month; steps down as nodes are committed.

Proposal mechanics I recommend we present:
1) External summary email with two-line bullets per option (clear table).
2) SOW draft to include an explicit migration clause: "pilot rates & support convert automatically to scale rates with specified notice and minimal administrative amendment" so procurement sees no full rewrite.
3) Offer a 20% pilot discount on node licensing for the first six months as a sign-of-good-faith (conditional on a 6–12 month conversion window).

Attachments included for client: pricing matrix (tabbed), SOW-draft-v2.pdf with the migration clause noted. Irene — please check the migration language and redline if necessary; Naomi, please bake the invoice milestones into the HubSpot deal notes so finance can map to POs.

Marissa
Head of Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: VPC implementation-gradient & volume discount pathway

Laura / team —

Appreciate the signal on capitalization and the pilot cap. Per Marissa’s update below, here are the two external-facing summaries we recommend. Short version + explicit next steps so procurement has what they need.

Option A — Anchor (recommended if you want the lowest unit economics at scale)
- Platform fee: $420,000 amortized 12 months (milestone: 30% on SOW execution, 40% after pilot acceptance, 30% monthly over remaining 9 months).
- Pilot node license: $2,800 / node / month (after 20% pilot discount applied) for first 6 months; scales to $2,200 / node / month at 8+ sites.
- Support: Pilot-level weekday SLA; scales to 24/7 with $45k/month retainer.
- Migration: Automatic conversion clause in SOW — no full contract rewrite required.

Option B — Elastic (if you must minimize up-front cash)
- Platform fee: $75,000 one-time (pilot cap).
- Pilot node license: $4,500 / node / month; volume discounts applied after month 6 and on committed nodes.
- Support: higher pilot retainer $28k/month; steps down with committed volume.

We are offering a 20% pilot discount on node licensing for the first six months on either option if Medisphere signs the pilot SOW within 14 days. Payment terms: Net45 available on Option A with an invoice schedule that preserves your accounting treatment (we'll map milestones to GAAP-friendly deliverables).

Next steps:
- David/Marissa: Send a one-page comparison (I’ll attach the matrix).
- Medisphere: Confirm preferred option and payment terms (Net30 vs Net45) + any PO reference.
- Procurement: If OK, we’ll push a final SOW for signature (DocuSign link will be shared).

For transparency: I’ve attached the working pricing matrix and SOW draft.

Best,
David
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-privdeploy-pricing-matrix.xlsx, SOW-draft-v2.pdf

Thanks for the clear options. We discussed internally and are broadly aligned with Option A (Anchor) provided you can:

1) Amend the invoice schedule so the majority of the platform fee is milestone-driven (we prefer 40% on pilot acceptance, remainder spread monthly).
2) Provide a line-item SOW that calls out acceptance criteria for the pilot (latency targets, throughput, uptime).
3) Confirm Net45 payment terms and include PO# MS-2026-1298 on the cover invoice.

If you can send the final SOW with the migration clause and the revised invoice schedule by EOD Monday we can route for signature.
